description.value: A double-blind, counter-balanced, within-subject pharmacological fMRI study examined whether intranasal oxytocin modulates cognitive control of food craving in healthy women.

To specifically examine the modulatory effects of OXT, a flexible factorial model was designed with the factors “treatment” (OXT, PLC) and “regulation” (LATER, NOW) to test the contrasts [(LATER OXT > NOW OXT ) > (LATER PLC > NOW PLC )] and [(NOW OXT > LATER OXT ) > (NOW PLC > LATER PLC )].

value: For LATER trials, OXT enhanced neural responses in several large clusters entailing the precuneus, cingulate cortex and precentral gyrus, and superior temporal gyrus. These findings indicate that OXT strengthened the neural circuitry involved in cognitive control of food craving.
